tool_targets.description: Generate images synchronously with gpt-image-2 through the official OpenAI Images API. Custom width and height must each be divisible by 16; use output_format png or webp for transparency.

model.description: Exact image model selected by this target.

prompt.description: Describe the requested image, composition, content, and style.

n.description: Number of images to return; every image is retained.

quality.description: Image rendering quality; xhigh and max require a GPT Image 2.5 model.

size.description: Use auto or WIDTHxHEIGHT. Each edge must be divisible by 16 and at most 3840 px. Aspect ratio must stay within 1:3 to 3:1. Total pixels must be 655360 through 8294400; above 3686400 pixels is experimental.

background.description: Select transparency explicitly. Transparent output requires PNG or WebP; GPT Image 2 transparency remains in preview.

output_compression.description: JPEG or WebP compression percentage. Omit for PNG; the API default for supported formats is 100.

safety_identifier.description: Optional pseudonymous end-user identifier for provider safety monitoring.

sources.note: The public Images Edits API accepts ordered reference images for GPT Image 2 and both GPT Image 2.5 models, with model-specific editing options.
The official Codex image tool sends GPT Image 2 edit requests with up to five input images.
The official Codex ImagesClient posts synchronous JSON to images/edits and decodes image data from the resulting JSON response.
Official ChatGPT Plan HTTP Responses contract and preview capability restrictions.
Official OpenAI model card for gpt-6.2-astra.
Official OpenAI model card for gpt-image-2.6-sunburst.
Official OpenAI model card for gpt-image-2.6-flare.
GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra use the public Responses route with the documented context, output, reasoning and structured output capabilities.
Codex CLI 0.170.0 model catalog supplies the distinct Responses Lite behavior and subscription reasoning levels. Authenticated discovery returned both model IDs at this client version.

GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst and Flare support generation, edits, complexity controls, transparent output, SVG and GIF preview. The Images API reference defines the JSON edit image locator, mask and markup shapes.
Codex subscription image generation follows the openai/codex ImagesClient request and response contract (codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/images.rs, model gpt-image-2).

The official client always sends size auto and exposes no size argument; live probes on 2026-10-24 requesting 1024x1024 all returned 1536x1024, so size is pinned to auto (openai/codex#43965 reports the same).

The user explicitly fixes the public API inventory to eight undated GPT-5.6, GPT-6 and GPT-6.1 conversation models. All use Responses, file/image input, low/medium/high/xhigh/max reasoning, 1050000 context and 128000 maximum output. API filtering is entry-scoped; Codex subscription declarations remain unchanged.

On 2026-11-08 the official model pages state that reasoning.effort supports none, low, medium (default), high, xhigh and max for GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, GPT-6 Sol/Luna and GPT-6.1 Terra, so those Responses rules add none. GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol list only low, medium, high, xhigh and max and stay unchanged. The Codex subscription rules are not covered by these pages and stay unchanged; no inference was tested.

On 2026-11-08 the official model pages of all eight public API conversation models (GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, GPT-6 Astra/Sol/Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol/Terra) list Structured outputs as Supported, and the guide states Structured Outputs (strict json_schema) and JSON mode work in both the Responses and Chat Completions APIs, recommending Structured Outputs over JSON mode. The Responses rules therefore declare json_schema. The Codex subscription endpoint is not covered by these documents and stays undeclared; no inference was tested.
Official Sol documentation supplies the shared 1050000 context, 128000 maximum output and reasoning levels adopted by the explicit user policy.

Authenticated read-only discovery on 2026-10-29 listed all eleven approved undated IDs. The endpoint reports identity and lifecycle fields only, so runtime membership intersects this exact allowlist; inference was not tested.

Official generation parameters define synchronous JSON requests, prompt length, n 1-10, output formats, conditional compression/transparency, safety identifier and per-model quality levels. GPT Image 2.5 adds xhigh/max; legacy style and response_format are excluded.
Custom dimensions require multiples of 16, edges no greater than 3840, aspect ratio within 1:3 and 3:1, and 655360-8294400 pixels. Outputs above 3686400 pixels are experimental.

On 2026-10-31 the user explicitly aligned the context declaration of all seven registered Codex subscription conversation models with the public API at 1050000 tokens. The previous 272000-token default must not be used as their model context ceiling. Session-level dynamic context-window selection and compaction remain independent and unchanged. Model inventory, output declarations and reasoning settings are unchanged. This supersedes the earlier unchanged-Codex scope note for context limits only; no live capacity test was performed.

Official guidance on 2026-11-03 recommends gpt-transcribe for recorded files on POST /audio/transcriptions: mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, wav and webm up to 25 MB, optional prompt, and stream=true emitting transcript.text.delta then transcript.text.done with text. whisper-1 and the gpt-4o transcribe models shut down on 2027-02-26 and are not registered.

The model page lists v1/audio/transcriptions as supported at 0.0045 USD per minute. The languages and keywords array fields are not projected because the multipart executor only sends scalar fields. Authenticated discovery on 2026-11-03 listed gpt-transcribe; no paid transcription was run for this declaration.
